title: KV pointer churn & eviction edge-case follow-up (slab fragmentation and transient corruption)
creator: Priya Nair
summary: Follow-up work after an incident where transient pointer churn caused slab fragmentation and evictions leading to capacity degradation under bursty load.
description:
What happened: During a mid-June capacity event, several hosts serving prefixcache experienced repeated pointer churn that accelerated slab fragmentation. Symptoms: sudden memory spikes, elevated eviction rates, and intermittent failed reads due to transient invalidation windows. Root-cause hypothesis: an insert/evict race combined with small-window allocator reuse that produced short-lived pointer recreation; in rare cases stale references were observed by readers before reclamation. This ticket captures experimental fixes, telemetry additions, and rollouts.

Goals: 1) Stop pointer-churn-driven fragmentation; 2) Prevent stale-read windows; 3) Improve observability to detect early signs; 4) Provide safe rollback paths and flags for emergency mitigation.

Proposed approach: A) Add epoch-based reclamation guard to allocator to avoid immediate reuse of recently-freed slab addresses for N seconds; B) Strengthen read path sanity checks and optional per-read checksum validation behind a feature flag for Canary; C) Implement eviction backpressure (slow eviction scoring decay) to avoid oscillation under burst; D) Add new metrics: pointer-reuse-rate, epoch-latency, raft-like republish-count for prefix manifests, slab-free-fragmentation-ratio.

Trade-offs: Epoch hold increases short-term memory usage; checksum validations add CPU overhead on reads — therefore both are gated behind rollout percentages and can be disabled for low-memory tiers. Eviction backpressure helps stability but may increase latency for cold keys; mitigation is bounded by policy (max backlog).
acceptance_criteria: No transient invalid reads in two full Canary clusters running high-burst replay for 72 hours
Pointer-reuse-rate metric drops to <= 0.01% under synthetic churn test
Eviction oscillation events (score flips) eliminated in monitored testbed for 7 days
All new telemetry dashboards in console with alerts and runbook created

2025-06-14 Ethan: Reproduced pointer churn in microbench with 16 concurrent inserters and TTLs of 2s. Hypothesis: allocator reuse within same slab. Implementing guarded free epoch locally.
2025-06-18 Alex: Checksum prototype added to read path behind flag; benchmarks show +4% CPU for 99th-percentile reads when enabled. Deciding to limit to Canary and low QPS reads first.
2025-06-21 Marta: Stress harness run #2: eviction oscillation reduced by tuning decay constant from 0.08 -> 0.02; fragmentation still increases slowly.
2025-06-25 Priya: Design review with SRE and Product. Agreed to accept temporary memory overhead for epoch guard to eliminate corruption risk. Product asked for tracking cost impact.
2025-06-30 SRE: Canary rollout to region eu-west-1 at 10% traffic. No invalid reads seen after 48h. Memory usage +6% on canaries, within toleration.
2025-07-01 Ethan: Opened PR #1248 for allocator guard and #1251 for eviction backpressure. Requesting engineering review and perf signoff.
